title.rendered: SHAPE Consortium Convenes partners meeting in Mombasa to Set the Course for Smart City Education in East Africa

content.rendered:
The Smart City Higher Education Advancement Programme in East Africa (SHAPE) has opened its international partners’ meeting in Mombasa, Kenya, running from September 28 to October 2, 2026. Co-funded by the European Union, SHAPE works to embed smart city concepts in university curricula, strengthen institutional capacity, and connect academic research with real urban innovation.

Hosted by Moi University, the meeting brings together university leaders, researchers, and innovation partners from across Africa and Europe. Participating institutions include the Open University of Kenya, Makerere University, the University of Tartu, Mogadishu University, Kampala International University, Red Sea University, Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg, a Lithuanian university, and Konza Technopolis. Over the course of the week, partners will align on shared objectives, launch key work packages, and map out the road ahead.

The opening day set the tone with a real sense of collaboration. Project Coordinator Prof. Kirimi Kiriamiti, joined by the vice-chancellors of Moi University and the Open University of Kenya, welcomed delegates on behalf of the host country institutions, followed by remarks from university representatives. The conversation then turned to the project’s vision, expected impact, and strategic direction. The day wrapped up with a visit to Fort Jesus, offering partners a warm introduction to Mombasa’s history.

Delegates also visited the Mama Ngina Waterfront, where the Indian Ocean setting offered a chance to connect over the coastal city that is hosting the work. The visit allowed partners to build the personal rapport that underpins effective international collaboration.

Through the remainder of the week, the consortium will hold technical sessions and collaborative workshops to advance smart city education across the region.

title.rendered: SHAPE Project Officially Launches: A New Partnership for Smart City Education in East Africa

content.rendered:
The Smart City Higher Education Advancement Program in East Africa (SHAPE) has officially launched, bringing together universities and industry partners from Kenya, Uganda, Somalia, Estonia, Germany, and Lithuania in a three-year collaboration to strengthen higher education for the future of African cities.

Funded by the European Union through the Erasmus+ Capacity Building in Higher Education (CBHE) programme and coordinated by Moi University in Kenya, SHAPE responds to a well-documented gap: according to UN-Habitat, 93% of local governments in Africa report skills shortages as a major barrier to smart city development, and only 29% of African cities currently have a smart city strategy in place.

Over the next three years, SHAPE aims to close that gap by equipping East African universities to design their own curricula, research, and training pipelines — built around the realities of their own cities rather than imported frameworks.

The official launch brought consortium partners together to establish a shared vision for the project and align on its implementation plan. Discussions centered on the role higher education institutions can play in developing the knowledge, skills, research, and innovation needed to support sustainable, inclusive, resilient, and technology-driven urban development across the region.

SHAPE unites institutions from across East Africa and Europe, each contributing distinct expertise.

Partner Universities

  1. Moi University (Kenya)
  2. Open University of Kenya (Kenya)
  3. Makerere University (Uganda)
  4. Kampala International University (Uganda)
  5. Mogadishu University (Somalia)
  6. Red Sea University (Somalia)
  7. Otto-von-Guericke-Universität Magdeburg (Germany)
  8. University of Tartu (Estonia)
  9. Lithuanian University of Health Sciences / LSMU (Lithuania)

Associated Partners

  1. Konza Technopolis Development Authority (Kenya)
  2. Université du Burundi (Burundi)
  3. Institute of Social Policy and Research (South Sudan)

These associated partners contribute to local case studies, inform curriculum design, and expand regional outreach beyond the primary consortium countries. Over its three-year run, SHAPE will strengthen academic cooperation between East Africa and Europe while transforming research into practical solutions for tomorrow’s urban centers.
